Observed facts: 60‑year‑old man with longstanding asthma, nasal polyps, chronic sinusitis and peak eosinophilia 3.8×10⁹/L. ANCA negative, prior biopsies showed no vasculitis; a clinical diagnosis of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) was made. Mepolizumab controlled disease for five years; stopped two years ago. Over the past year asthma and sinus symptoms recurred. Seven months ago right facial pain began; five months ago bilateral facial weakness improved with steroids; three months ago painful right visual loss improved after prednisone and doxycycline (unclear which agent). After tapering prednisone from 30 mg to 20 mg, right V2 pain and sensory loss persisted. Outside MRI highlighted small‑vessel and sinus changes; institutional review notes multifocal dural enhancement. No later cardiac data or treatment response are available.

Hypotheses: 1) EGPA relapse with cranial‑nerve and dural involvement despite negative ANCA. 2) Separate inflammatory disorder such as neurosarcoidosis or idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis producing similar dural enhancement. 3) Infectious or neoplastic process (e.g., invasive fungal sinusitis, lymphoma) mimicking vasculitic features.

Provisional assessment: The historic EGPA label, prior eosinophilia, and steroid‑responsive cranial neuropathies favor an EGPA flare, but negative ANCA and lack of histologic vasculitis lower certainty. Multifocal dural enhancement argues for a meningeal inflammatory process that may be EGPA‑related or distinct. Urgent further review should include repeat high‑resolution MRI with contrast, lumbar puncture for cytology, flow cytometry, ACE, and infectious panels, and consideration of tissue biopsy of enhancing dura or sinus mucosa. Re‑initiation of high‑dose steroids and mepolizumab should be weighed after these results.
